text: When you write code, you will inevitably encounter bugs. Identifying bugs begins with understanding what your program is supposed to do. A systematic approach helps you find errors efficiently. First, reproduce the bug consistently. Then, narrow down the problem area by checking your code step by step. Debugging tools, such as breakpoints in an IDE, let you pause and inspect variables. Logging is another powerful strategy. By adding print statements or using a logging library, you can track your program's flow and spot unexpected values. Start with clear assumptions, test each one, and you will solve most issues methodically.
